description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Signals and Systems topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: signals-systems

facts.claim: Linearity = superposition

source.quote: The latter condition is often referred to as the superposition principle

facts.claim: An LTI system is fully described by its impulse response

source.quote: LTI systems can be characterized entirely by a single function called the system's impulse response

facts.claim: Output when the input is an impulse

source.quote: of a dynamic system is its output when presented with a brief input signal

facts.claim: Output for any input follows from input and impulse response

source.quote: for any input, the output can be calculated in terms of the input and the impulse response

facts.claim: Integral of the product after one is reflected and shifted

source.quote: the integral of the product of the two functions after one is reflected about the y-axis and shifted

facts.claim: A periodic signal is a sum of sines and cosines

source.quote: A Fourier series () is a series expansion of a periodic function into a sum of trigonometric functions

facts.claim: Output is a (complex) function of frequency

source.quote: The output of the transform is a complex valued function of frequency

facts.claim: Narrow in time means spread out in frequency

source.quote: Functions that are localized in the time domain have Fourier transforms that are spread out across the frequency domain and vice versa

facts.claim: Magnitude and phase of the output versus frequency

source.quote: the quantitative measure of the magnitude and phase of the output as a function of input

facts.claim: Magnitude often in decibels

source.quote: typically in decibels (dB)

facts.claim: Laplace transform maps time to the complex s-domain

source.quote: (in the complex-valued frequency domain, also known as s-domain or s-plane)

facts.claim: Turns differential equations into algebra

source.quote: mostly as a tool for solving linear differential equations and dynamical systems

facts.claim: Converts a discrete-time sequence into the z-domain

source.quote: the Z-transform converts a discrete-time signal, which is a sequence of real or complex numbers

facts.claim: Discrete-time counterpart of the Laplace transform

source.quote: It can be considered a discrete-time counterpart of the Laplace transform

facts.claim: Sample at more than twice the highest frequency (Nyquist)

source.quote: An important consequence of the sampling theorem is the concept of Nyquist frequency

facts.claim: Applies to band-limited signals

source.quote: the class of functions that are band-limited to a given bandwidth

facts.claim: Reconstructed signal differs from the original (distortion)

source.quote: It also often refers to the distortion or artifact that results when a signal reconstructed from samples is different from the original continuous signal

facts.claim: The DTFT applies to a sequence of discrete values

source.quote: the discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT) is a form of Fourier analysis that is applicable to a sequence of discrete values

facts.claim: The DTFT is periodic in frequency

source.quote: it produces a function of frequency that is a periodic summation of the continuous Fourier transform

facts.claim: State variables with first-order differential equations

source.quote: a mathematical model of a physical system that uses state variables to track how inputs shape system behavior over time

facts.claim: A zero-order hold keeps each sample value for one sample interval

source.quote: by holding each sample value for one sample interval
